about: This part finishes the third day and tells the fourth, and the fifth begins. If the dead man does not recognise Ratnasambhava's yellow light as the radiance of his own awareness, he is to take refuge in it, turn away from the dull blue light of humans and its sufferings of birth, age, sickness and death, and say the prayer to Ratnasambhava; then he becomes a buddha in the southern realm. Some, great wrongdoers and those whose commitments are broken, still do not recognise it and flee, and on the fourth day the element fire dawns as a red light: from the western realm of Bliss Amitābha appears on a peacock throne, in union with the White-Robed One and surrounded by two bodhisattvas and two female bodhisattvas, and his red discriminating wisdom comes together with the dull yellow light of the hungry ghosts. He is to rest in awareness or, failing that, take refuge, give up desire and pray to Amitābha, and so become a buddha in the west. Those who have long kept company with their habitual tendencies are driven by jealousy and bad karma to wander on, and on the fifth day the element wind dawns as a green light: the part ends as Amoghasiddhi appears from the northern realm on a throne of shang-shang birds, in union with Samayatārā, while the light of the demigods comes too.

sentences.w: རང་ གི་ རིག་པའི་ རང་མདངས་སུ་ མ་ ཤེས་ ན་ ནི༔ བཅོམ་ལྡན་འདས་ རིན་ཆེན་འབྱུང་ལྡན་ གྱི་ ཐུགས་རྗེའི་ འོད་ཟེར་ ཡིན་ནོ་ སྐྱབས་སུ་ མཆིའོ་ སྙམ་པའི་ མོས་གུས་ གྱིས་ ལ་ གསོལ་བ་ ཐོབ་ཅིག༔
sentences.l: Oneself's knowing's as-own-radiance not know if, as-for: 'The Blessed-One Ratnasambhava's compassion's light-ray it-is; for-refuge I-go' thinking's devotion-respect do, and, prayer obtain(?)!
sentences.i: If you do not recognise it as the natural radiance of your own awareness, think with devotion, 'This is the light of the compassion of the Blessed One Ratnasambhava; I go to it for refuge', and pray.
sentences.n: The first words stand on p. 45 after the last sentence of the part before, which gave the case of recognition; this is the other case. rang gi, 'one's own', where that sentence had khyod rang gi, 'your own'; the other recension has ngo ma shes na ni, with ngo, 'face', as in ngo shes. The refuge formula is the one of the first and second days, with Ratnasambhava's name and mos gus, 'devotion and respect', for mos pa; gsol ba thob cig is read, as there, as a guess for 'pray'.

sentences.w: དེ་ ནི་ བཅོམ་ལྡན་འདས་ རིན་ཆེན་འབྱུང་ལྡན་ ཁྱོད་ བར་དོའི་ འཇིགས་སྐྲག་ ལ་ བསུ་བ་ འོང་བ་ ཡིན་ནོ༔
sentences.l: That, as-for: the Blessed-One Ratnasambhava, you, the between's terror in, meeting coming it-is.
sentences.i: That is the Blessed One Ratnasambhava coming to meet you in the terrors of the bardo.
sentences.n: The sentence of the second day, with two differences: here the print has de ni, 'that is', for de nas, 'then', and the terror of the bardo ('jigs skrag) for its narrow passage, the two readings the other recension had there. 'ong ba, 'coming', the present stem, stands for 'ongs pa, 'has come', and there is no la after bsu ba: 'is coming to meet you'.

sentences.w: རིན་ཆེན་འབྱུང་ལྡན་ གྱི་ ཐུགས་རྗེའི་ འོད་ཟེར་ གྱི་ ལྕགས་ཀྱུ་ ཡིན་བའི་ མོས་པ་ གྱིས་ཤིག༔
sentences.l: Ratnasambhava's compassion's light-ray's iron-hook being's devotion do!
sentences.i: Turn with devotion to it as the hook of the light of Ratnasambhava's compassion.
sentences.n: yin ba'i is the print's spelling of yin pa'i, 'which is': the clause describes the devotion, one that takes the light for the hook. On the second day the print had yin pas, 'because it is', and the other recension has yin pas here: 'it is the hook, so turn to it with devotion'.

sentences.w: མིའི་ འོད་ སྔོན་པོ་ བཀྲག་མེད་ དེ་ ལ་ དགའ་བར་ མ་ བྱེད་ཅིག༔
sentences.l: Humans' light, blue, lustreless, that in, delight not do!
sentences.i: Do not take delight in the dull blue light of humans.
sentences.n: As on the second day, with the light of humans, which the print makes blue.

sentences.w: ཁྱོད་ ཀྱི་ ང་རྒྱལ་ དྲག་པོས་ བསགས་པའི་ བག་ཆགས་ ཀྱི་ བསུ་བའི་ ལམ་ ཡིན་ནོ༔
sentences.l: Your pride fierce-by accumulated's habitual-tendencies' welcoming's path it-is.
sentences.i: It is the path on which the habitual tendencies gathered by your fierce pride come out to meet you.
sentences.n: As on the second day, with the third day's poison, pride. The print has no de, 'that', at the head of the sentence; the other recension has it, and has bag chags kyis bsu ma'i 'od lam, 'the light-path of the welcomer, by the tendencies', where the print has the path.

sentences.w: དེ་ ལ་ ཆགས་ ན་ ནི་ ཁྱོད་ མིའི་ གནས་སུ་ ལྟུང་ ནས་ སྐྱེ་ རྒ་ ན་ འཆིའི་ སྡུག་བསྔལ་ ཉམས་སུ་མྱོང་ ཞིང་ འཁོར་བའི་ འདམ་ ནས་ ཐོན་པའི་ དུས་ མི་ འབྱུང་ སྟེ༔
sentences.l: That to attached if, as-for: you, humans' abode-to fall, then; birth, age, sickness, death's suffering experience, and; saṃsāra's mire from getting-out's time not comes, and:
sentences.i: If you are attached to it, you will fall into the abode of humans and go through the suffering of birth, old age, sickness and death, and the time of getting out of the mire of saṃsāra will not come.
sentences.n: mi'i gnas, 'the abode of humans', where this day's dull light leads. ltung, 'to fall', is the print's spelling here of lhung, which it writes on the second day and below. skye rga na 'chi, 'birth, ageing, sickness and death', the four great sufferings of a human life: na here is 'to be ill' (na ba), not the particle 'if'. nyams su myong, 'to experience, to go through', one word as nyams su blangs, 'to put into practice', in the pilot. 'dam, 'mud, mire', as on the second day; thon, 'to get out, to emerge'. The other recension has 'the time of being freed from the place of saṃsāra' ('khor ba'i gnas nas thar ba'i dus).

sentences.w: ཐར་པའི་ ལམ་ བཀག་པའི་ བར་ཆད་ ཡིན་པས་ དེ་ ལ་ མིག་ མི་ བལྟ་བར་ ང་རྒྱལ་ སྤོངས་ཤིག༔
sentences.l: Liberation's path blocked's obstacle it-is-because: that at eye not looking-way, pride abandon!
sentences.i: It is an obstacle that blocks the path to liberation, so do not look at it; give up your pride.
sentences.n: bkag pa'i, 'blocking', is the past stem of 'gog, 'to block', where the days before had the future dgag pa'i; the sense is the same. mig mi blta bar, 'without looking', has mi where the second day had ma. As there, the poison itself is to be given up.

sentences.w: བག་ཆགས་ སྤོངས་ཤིག༔ མ་ ཆགས་ཤིག༔ མ་ ཞེན་ཅིག༔
sentences.l: Habitual-tendencies abandon! Not be-attached! Not cling!
sentences.i: Give up your habitual tendencies. Do not be attached; do not cling.
sentences.n: Not only the pride but the tendencies it has laid down are to be given up.

sentences.w: འོད་ སེར་པོ་ སེར་ ལ་ མཚེར་བ་ དེ་ ལ་ མོས་པ་ གྱིས་ཤིག༔
sentences.l: Light yellow, yellow and shimmering, that to devotion do!
sentences.i: Turn with devotion to the yellow light, yellow and shimmering.
sentences.n: mtsher ba is read as 'tsher ba, 'shimmering', as in the last part. The other recension has gsal la 'tsher ba, 'bright and shimmering', and runs on with gyis la, 'and'.

sentences.w: བཅོམ་ལྡན་འདས་ རིན་ཆེན་འབྱུང་ལྡན་ ལ་ འདུན་པ་ རྩེ་གཅིག་ཏུ་ གཏོད་ ལ་ སྨོན་ལམ་ འདི་སྐད་དུ་ ཐོབ་ཅིག༔
sentences.l: The Blessed-One Ratnasambhava to aspiration one-pointedly direct, and; prayer these-words-in obtain(?)!
sentences.i: Direct a single-minded longing to the Blessed One Ratnasambhava, and make this prayer:
sentences.n: rtse gcig tu, 'one-pointedly' (rtse, 'point, tip'; gcig, 'one'), where the days before had drag po, 'fierce'. smon lam 'di skad du thob cig is read, as on the second day, as a guess for 'make this prayer'.

sentences.w: ཀྱཻ་མ་ ང་རྒྱལ་ དྲག་པོས་ འཁོར་བར་ འཁྱམས་པའི་ ཚེ༔ / མཉམ་ཉིད་ ཡེ་ཤེས་ གསལ་བའི་ འོད་ལམ་ ལ༔ / བཅོམ་ལྡན་ རིན་ཆེན་འབྱུང་ལྡན་ ལམ་སྣ་ དྲོངས༔ / ཡུམ་ མཆོག་ མཱ་མ་ཀི་ ཡི་ རྒྱབ་ ནས་ བསྐྱོར༔ / བར་དོ་ འཇིགས་པའི་ འཕྲང་ ལས་ བསྒྲལ་དུ་ གསོལ༔ / ཡང་དག་ རྫོགས་པའི་ སངས་རྒྱས་ ས་རུ་ སྐྱོལ༔
sentences.l:
Alas! Pride fierce-by in-saṃsāra wandering's time,
the sameness wisdom bright's light-path on,
the Blessed-One Ratnasambhava the-way lead!
The mother supreme Māmakī of(by?) from-behind support!
The between fearful's narrow-passage from freeing I-pray;
the genuine perfect buddha's level-to bring!
sentences.i:
Alas! When I wander in saṃsāra through fierce pride,
on the bright light-path of the wisdom of sameness
may the Blessed One Ratnasambhava lead the way,
may the supreme mother Māmakī support me from behind.
I pray you, free me from the fearful narrow passage of the bardo
and bring me to the level of a true and perfect buddha.
sentences.n: The prayer of the first two days, with the third day's poison, wisdom, buddha and consort. mnyam nyid ye shes is mnyam pa nyid kyi ye shes, 'the wisdom of sameness', shortened for the metre. mA ma ki yi has yi, 'of', where the line wants yis, 'by', as the first day's consort has it and the other recension has here: 'from behind Māmakī' gives little sense, and it is read as 'by'. bskyor, past and future stem of skyor, 'hold up', as on the second day; skyol, 'bring!', as on the first.

sentences.w: དེ་སྐད་ མོས་གུས་ དྲག་པོས་ སྨོན་ལམ་ བཏབ་པས༔ བཅོམ་ལྡན་འདས་ རིན་ཆེན་འབྱུང་ལྡན་ གྱི་ ཐུགས་ཀར་ འཇའ་འོད་དུ་ ཐིམ་ ནས༔ ལྷོ་ཕྱོགས་ དཔལ་ དང་ ལྡན་པའི་ ཞིང་ཁམས་སུ་ ལོངས་སྤྱོད་རྫོགས་པའི་སྐུར་ སངས་རྒྱས་པར་ འགྱུར་རོ༔
sentences.l: Those-words, devotion-respect fierce-by, prayer made-because: the Blessed-One Ratnasambhava's heart-in as-rainbow-light dissolving, then, the south-direction, Glory-with-Endowed's realm-in, as-the-body-of-perfect-enjoyment buddha becomes.
sentences.i: When he makes the prayer in these words with fierce devotion, he dissolves as rainbow light into the heart of the Blessed One Ratnasambhava and becomes a buddha in the body of perfect enjoyment in the southern realm Endowed with Glory.
sentences.n: As on the first two days. de skad, 'those words', stands first here, without the zhes, 'thus', that closed the prayer there. The other recension has the heart of Ratnasambhava and his consort (yab yum).

sentences.w: དེ་ལྟར་དུ་ ངོ་སྤྲད་པས་ དབང་པོ་ ཇི་ལྟར་ གཞན་ ཡང་ གྲོལ་བར་ ཐེ་ཚོམ་ མེད་དོ༔
sentences.l: Thus face-introduced-because: faculties however, others(?) also, freed-to doubt there-is-not.
sentences.i: When he is pointed out in this way, there is no doubt that he will be freed, however weak his faculties.
sentences.n: dbang po, 'faculty', a person's capacity for the teaching. The print has gzhan yang, 'others too' (gzhan, 'other'; yang, 'also'), which gives no clear sense after ji ltar, 'however'; the other recension has ji ltar zhan kyang, 'however weak (zhan) they are', and the sentence is translated by that sense. The letters of the print are clear, and how its reading came about cannot be told, so it is kept; the translation of these words is uncertain. The print writes med do contracted (མེདོ); it is written out here, as the print's other contractions are.

sentences.w: ཡང་ དེ་ལྟར་ ལན་མང་དུ་ ངོ་སྤྲད་ ཀྱང་ སྡིག་པོ་ཆེ་ ལ་སོགས་པ་ དང༔ དམ་ཚིག་ ཉམས་པ་ ལ་སོགས་པའི་ སྐལ་ཆད་ ཀྱི་ རིགས་ ལ་ ད་དུང་ ཡང་ ངོ་ མི་ འཕྲོད་པའི་ རིགས་ འོང་ སྟེ༔
sentences.l: Again, thus many-times face-introduced though: great-wrongdoers and-so-on, and; commitment broken and-so-on's fortune-cut-off's kind among, still even, face not meeting's kind comes, and:
sentences.i: But though they are pointed out many times in this way, among those cut off from fortune, great wrongdoers and the like and those whose sacred commitments are broken and the like, there are some who still do not recognise it.
sentences.n: lan mang du, 'many times'. sdig po che, 'a great wrongdoer'; the other recension has mi sdig po che, 'a person of great wrongdoing'. dam tshig, 'sacred commitment' (Sanskrit samaya), the bond with the teacher and the practice that a disciple takes on; nyams pa, 'broken'. skal chad, 'cut off from fortune', one who lacks the good fortune to be helped by the teaching. rigs, 'kind, sort': skal chad kyi rigs la ... ngo mi 'phrod pa'i rigs 'ong, 'among the luckless sort there come some who do not recognise'. da dung yang, 'even now, still'.

sentences.w: འདོད་ཆགས་ དང་ སྡིག་སྒྲིབ་ ཀྱིས་ བསྐྱོད་ ནས་ སྒྲ་ འོད་ ལ་ འཇིགས་ ཏེ་ བྲོས་བས༔
sentences.l: Desire and sin-obscuration by stirred, then, sound, light at fearing, and, fled-because:
sentences.i: Stirred by desire and sinful obscurations, they are afraid of the sounds and lights and flee. So
sentences.n: 'dod chags, 'desire, passion', is the poison of the fourth day. bskyod, 'stirred, set in motion', past of skyod. bros bas is the print's spelling of bros pas, 'because they flee', which runs on to what happens next.

sentences.w: ཞག་ བཞི་པ་ ལ༔ བཅོམ་ལྡན་འདས་ སྣང་བ་མཐའ་ཡས་ ཀྱི་ ལྷ་ཚོགས་ དང༔ འདོད་ཆགས་ དང་ སེར་སྣ་ ལས་ གྲུབ་པའི་ ཡི་དྭགས་ ལ་ འོད་ལམ་ གཉིས་ ཀྱིས་ བསུ་བ་ ལ་ འོང་ སྟེ༔
sentences.l: Day fourth on: the Blessed-One Amitābha's deity-host and; desire and avarice from formed's hungry-ghosts with(?), light-paths two by, meeting for come, and:
sentences.i: on the fourth day the host of deities of the Blessed One Amitābha and the hungry ghosts, formed from desire and avarice, come to meet them as two light-paths.
sentences.n: Snang ba mtha' yas, 'Boundless Appearance, Boundless Light' (Sanskrit Amitābha; snang ba, 'appearance, light'; mtha' yas, 'without end'), is the buddha of the west and of the fourth day. ser sna, 'avarice, stinginess'. grub pa, 'formed, made of'. yi dwags, 'hungry ghost' (Sanskrit preta), a being tormented by hunger and thirst, the realm this day's dull light leads to. yi dwags la has la where kyi, 'of', would be expected (the other recension has yi dwags kyi 'od lam, 'the light-path of the hungry ghosts'); the print's la is clear on the image, and the sentence is read as 'the host and the hungry ghosts, two light-paths'.

sentences.w: ཡང་ ངོ་སྤྲད་པ་ ནི༔ ཚེ་འདས་ ཀྱི་ མིང་ ནས་ བོད་ ལ་ འདི་སྐད་དོ༔ ཀྱཻ་ རིགས་ཀྱི་བུ་ མ་ ཡེངས་པར་ ཉོན་ཅིག༔
sentences.l: Again, the face-introduction, as-for: the dead-one's by-name calling, and, these-words: O child-of-noble-family, not distracted-way listen!
sentences.i: Point him out again. Call the dead person by name and say this: O child of noble family, listen without distraction.
sentences.n: As on the second and third days. bod is the print's spelling here of 'bod, 'to call', which it writes in the same formula on the fifth day below; bod is a known variant of the verb.

sentences.w: ཞག་ བཞི་པ་ ལ་ འབྱུང་བ་ མེ་ རྣམ་པར་ དག་པའི་ འོད་ དམར་པོ་ འཆར་རོ༔
sentences.l: Day fourth on, element fire completely pure's light, red, dawns.
sentences.i: On the fourth day the red light dawns, the light of the element fire, wholly purified.
sentences.n: me, 'fire'; dmar po, 'red'. Here the print has no thams cad, 'all', which it has on the second, third and fifth days.

sentences.w: དེའི་ དུས་སུ་ ནུབ་ཕྱོགས་ བདེ་བ་ཅན་ གྱི་ ཞིང་ཁམས་ དམར་པོ་ ནས༔ བཅོམ་ལྡན་འདས་ སྣང་བ་མཐའ་ཡས་ སྐུ་མདོག་ དམར་པོ༔ ཕྱག་ ན་ པདྨ་ བསྣམས་པ་ རྨ་བྱའི་ གདན་ ལ་ བཞུགས་པ༔
sentences.l: That's time-at, the west-direction, the-Blissful's realm, red, from: the Blessed-One Amitābha, body-colour red, hand in lotus holding, peacock's seat on seated,
sentences.i: At that time, from the red western realm of Bliss, the Blessed One Amitābha, red in colour, holding a lotus in his hand and seated on a peacock throne,
sentences.n: nub phyogs, 'the west'. Bde ba can, 'the Blissful' (Sanskrit Sukhāvatī; bde ba, 'bliss'; can, 'having'), is the buddha-field of the west. padma, 'lotus', is Sanskrit in stacked Tibetan letters. rma bya, 'peacock'.

sentences.w: ཡུམ་ མཆོག་ གོས་དཀར་མོ་ དང་ ཞལ་སྦྱར་ ནས་ རང་ ལ་ འཆར་དུ་ འོང་ངོ༔
sentences.l: The mother supreme White-Robed-One with face-joined, then, oneself to dawning comes.
sentences.i: in union with the supreme consort, the White-Robed One, dawns before you.
sentences.n: Gos dkar mo, 'the White-Robed One' (Sanskrit Pāṇḍaravāsinī; gos, 'clothing'; dkar mo, 'white', with the feminine -mo), is the consort of the west.

sentences.w: བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའ་ སྤྱན་རས་གཟིགས་ དང༔ འཇམ་དཔལ་ གཉིས་ ལ༔ སེམས་མ་ གྷཱིརྟི་མ་ དང་༔ ཨཱ་ལོ་ཀེ་ གཉིས་ ཀྱིས་ བསྐོར་ ནས་ འཇའ་འོད་ ཀྱིས་ ཀློང་ ནས་ སངས་རྒྱས་ ཀྱི་ སྐུ་ དྲུག་ཏུ་ འཆར་ ནས་ འོང་ངོ༔
sentences.l: The bodhisattva Avalokita and Mañjuśrī, two, with; the female-bodhisattvas Gītā and Ālokā, two, by surrounded, then: rainbow-light by(?) expanse from, buddha's bodies six-as dawning come.
sentences.i: Surrounded by the two bodhisattvas Avalokiteśvara and Mañjuśrī and the two female bodhisattvas Gītā and Ālokā, they come, dawning as six buddha forms out of an expanse of rainbow light.
sentences.n: Spyan ras gzigs, 'the one who looks with the eyes' (Avalokiteśvara), is the bodhisattva of compassion; 'Jam dpal, 'Gentle Glory' (Mañjuśrī), the bodhisattva of wisdom. The female bodhisattvas' names are Sanskrit in Tibetan letters: the print writes གྷཱིརྟི་མ (ghīrti ma) for Gītā, 'she of song' (the other recension has གིརྟི), and ཨཱ་ལོ་ཀེ (ā lo ke) for Ālokā, 'she of the lamp' (the other recension ཨཱ་ལོ་མ). 'ja' 'od kyis klong has kyis, 'by', where kyi, 'of', is meant (the other recension has kyi); the print is kept and read so, as with sangs rgyas kyis in the last part.

sentences.w: འདུ་ཤེས་ ཀྱི་ ཕུང་པོ་ གནས་སུ་ དག་པ༔ འོད་ དམར་པོ་ སོ་སོར་ རྟོགས་བའི་ ཡེ་ཤེས་ དམར་ ལ་ འཚེར་བ་ ཐིག་ལེ་ དང་ ཐིག་ཕྲན་ གྱིས་ བརྒྱན་པ༔ གསལ་ ལ་ དྭངས་པ༔
sentences.l: Perception's aggregate in-its-place pure: light red, individually discerning's wisdom, red and shimmering, drops and small-drops by adorned, bright and clear,
sentences.i: The aggregate of perception, pure in its own place, is the red light, the discriminating wisdom: red and shimmering, adorned with drops and smaller drops, bright and clear,
sentences.n: 'du shes, 'perception', the third aggregate, the mind's taking of a thing as this or that; it is the word rendered 'notion' in the last part. so sor rtogs pa'i ye shes, 'the wisdom that discerns each thing by itself' (so sor, 'one by one'; rtogs, 'to understand'; Sanskrit pratyavekṣaṇājñāna), is the wisdom of Amitābha; rtogs ba'i is the print's spelling of rtogs pa'i. Here the print writes 'tsher with its proper first letter. As on the second day the print closes the aggregate with dag pa and ༔; the other recension has dag pa'i 'od dmar po, 'the red light which is the aggregate made pure'.

sentences.w: བཀྲག་ ལ་ འཚེར་བ་ གཅིག་ སྣང་བ་མཐའ་ཡས་ ཡབ་ཡུམ་ གྱི་ ཐུགས་ཀ་ ནས༔ ཁྱོད་རང་ གི་ སྙིང་ གི་ ཐད་ཀར་ མིག་ གིས་ མི་ བཟོད་པ་ ཙམ་དུ་ ཟུག་ ནས་ འོང་ངོ༔
sentences.l: lustrous and shimmering, one, Amitābha father-mother's heart from, you-yourself's heart's straight-at, eye by not bearable as-much-as, piercing comes.
sentences.i: a lustrous, shimmering light, it comes piercing from the heart of Amitābha and his consort straight at your heart, so bright that your eyes can hardly bear it.
sentences.n: The print has ཐད་དཀར, a misprint for ཐད་ཀར, 'straight at', corrected here: dkar is 'white', which gives no sense, the print has thad kar in the same phrase on the third day, and the other recension has it here. The tsheg between pa and tsam in mi bzod pa tsam du cannot be seen on the image, where the heads of the two letters touch; the reading pa tsam, which the sense needs and the print has in the same phrase on the third day, is taken, but it is uncertain.

sentences.w: དེ་ ལ་ མ་ འཇིགས་ཤིག༔
sentences.l: That at, not fear!
sentences.i: Do not be afraid of it.
sentences.n: ma 'jigs shig, 'do not fear', as in the warnings of 003 when the bardo of reality dawns.

sentences.w: དེ་ དང་ མཉམ་དུ་ ཡི་དྭགས་ ཀྱི་ འོད་ སེར་པོ་ བཀྲག་མེད་པ་ ཅིག་ ཀྱང༔ ཡེ་ཤེས་ ཀྱི་ འོད་ དང་ གཤིབས་མར་ ཁྱོད་ ལ་ འཆར་དུ་ འོང་བས༔ དེ་ ལ་ དགའ་བར་ མ་ བྱེད་ཅིག༔ ཆགས་ཞེན་ སྤོངས་ཤིག༔
sentences.l: That with together, hungry-ghosts' light, yellow, lustreless, one, also, wisdom's light with side-by-side, you to dawning comes-because: that in delight not do! Attachment-clinging abandon!
sentences.i: Together with it a dull yellow light, the light of the hungry ghosts, also dawns before you, side by side with the light of wisdom. Do not take delight in it; give up attachment and clinging.
sentences.n: The print has བཀྲག་མད་པ, a misprint for བཀྲག་མེད་པ, 'lustreless', corrected here: the vowel sign is missing, the print writes bkrag med in the same phrase a few lines below and on the third day, and the other recension has bkrag med pa. cig is the print's form of zhig, 'a, one', as before. 'ong bas, 'because it comes', runs on to the commands. chags zhen, 'attachment and clinging', the two verbs of the days before made one word.

sentences.w: དེའི་ དུས་སུ་ ཁྱོད་ འདོད་ཆགས་ དྲག་པོའི་ དབང་ གིས༔ འོད་ དམར་པོ་ བཀྲག་མདངས་ཅན་ དེ་ ལ་ ཁྱོད་ སྐྲག་པ་ སྐྱེས་ ནས་ བྲོས་སུ་ འོངས་ ཤིང་༔
sentences.l: That's time-at, you, desire fierce's power by, light red lustre-radiance-having, that, at, you, fright having-arisen, fleeing came, and:
sentences.i: At that time, driven by fierce desire, you will be frightened of the lustrous, radiant red light and flee from it,
sentences.n: As on the third day, with the poison of this day. 'ongs, the past of 'ong, stands where the third day had 'ong gis; with bros su it says what will happen, as there. As on the second day the print has a second khyod, 'you', which the other recension lacks.

sentences.w: ཡི་དྭགས་ ཀྱི་ འོད་ སེར་པོ་ བཀྲག་མེད་ དེ་ ལ་ ཁྱོད་ དགའ་བ་ དང་ ཆགས་སེམས་ བསྐྱེད་ ནས་ འོང་ གིས༔
sentences.l: Hungry-ghosts' light, yellow, lustreless, that toward, you, delight and attachment-mind having-produced, come, and:
sentences.i: and you will feel delight and desire for the dull yellow light of the hungry ghosts and go toward it.
sentences.n: bskyed, 'produced, made to arise', is the past of skyed, the active partner of skye, 'to arise': the third day had skyes, 'arose', and the other recension has skyes here. 'ong gis runs on, as there.

sentences.w: དེ་ཙ་ན་ ཁྱོད་ འོད་ དམར་པོ་ བཀྲག་ ལ་ འཚེར་བ་ གསལ་ ལ་ དྭངས་པ་ དེ་ ལ་ མ་ འཇིགས་པར་ ཡེ་ཤེས་སུ་ ངོ་ ཤེས་པར་ གྱིས་ཤིག༔
sentences.l: At-that-time, you, light red, lustrous and shimmering, bright and clear, that at not fearing-way, as-wisdom face-knowing do!
sentences.i: At that time do not be afraid of the red light, lustrous and shimmering, bright and clear: recognise it as wisdom.
sentences.n: As on the days before.

sentences.w: དེའི་ ཐོག་ཏུ་ རིགས་པ་ བྱར་མེད་ ཀྱི་ ངང་དུ་ གློད་ ལ་ ཞོག་ཅིག༔
sentences.l: That's on-top, knowing nothing-to-do's state-in loosen, and, rest!
sentences.i: Then relax and rest in the state of awareness where there is nothing to do.
sentences.n: de'i thog tu, 'upon that, thereupon' (thog, 'top'). rigs pa is the print's spelling here of rig pa, 'awareness', as once in 002; rigs pa as a word by itself is 'reasoning', which gives no sense here, and the print writes rig pa in the same phrase on the third day. ngang du, 'in the state', where the third day had ngang la. zhog, the imperative of 'jog, 'to leave, to put', where the third day had bzhogs shig.

sentences.w: དབྱེར་མེད་དུ་ ཐིམ་ ནས་ སངས་རྒྱས་པར་ འགྱུར་རོ༔
sentences.l: Inseparable-as dissolving, then, buddha become.
sentences.i: Dissolving inseparably, you will become a buddha.
sentences.n: Here the print lacks a passage that the other recension has, and that the print itself has in the same place on the third day: after zhog cig it goes straight on to dbyer med du thim nas, where the other has 'Or else, turn to it with faith and devotion, longingly. If you recognise it as your own radiance, then even without devotion and without making the prayer, all the forms and lights (dissolve) inseparably into you yourself', and then 'dissolving, you become a buddha'. A carver may have skipped from one stretch to a like one; the print is followed, and its sentence still reads, though what dissolves is not named.

sentences.w: དེ་ལྟར་ མ་ ཤེས་ ན༔ བཅོམ་ལྡན་འདས་ སྣང་བ་མཐའ་ཡས་ ཀྱི་ ཐུགས་རྗེའི་ འོད་ཟེར་ ཡིན་ནོ་ སྐྱབས་སུ་ མཆིའོ་ སྙམ་པའི་ མོས་གུས་ གྱིས་ ལ་ གསོལ་བ་ ཐོབ་ཅིག༔
sentences.l: Thus not know if: 'The Blessed-One Amitābha's compassion's light-ray it-is; for-refuge I-go' thinking's devotion-respect do, and, prayer obtain(?)!
sentences.i: If you do not recognise it so, think with devotion, 'This is the light of the compassion of the Blessed One Amitābha; I go to it for refuge', and pray.
sentences.n: As at the beginning of this part, with Amitābha's name.

sentences.w: དེ་ ནི་ བཅོམ་ལྡན་འདས་ སྣང་བ་མཐའ་ཡས་ ཀྱིས་ ཐུགས་རྗེའི་ འོད་ཟེར་ གྱི་ ལྕགས་ཀྱུ་ ཡིན་ནོ་ མོས་པ་ གྱིས་ཤིག༔
sentences.l: That, as-for: the Blessed-One Amitābha's(by?) compassion's light-ray's iron-hook it-is; devotion do!
sentences.i: It is the hook of the light of the compassion of the Blessed One Amitābha: turn to it with devotion.
sentences.n: snang ba mtha' yas kyis has kyis, 'by', where kyi, 'of', is meant (the other recension has kyi); it is read so. yin no, 'it is', runs straight on to the command with no mark between, as in the refuge formula. The other recension has thugs rje lcags kyu'i 'od zer, 'the rays of the hook of compassion'.

sentences.w: མ་ བྲོས་ཅིག༔ བྲོས་ ཀྱང་ ཁྱོད་རང་ དང་ འདུ་འབྲལ་ མེད་པར་ འོང་ངོ༔ མ་ འཇིགས་ཤིག༔
sentences.l: Not flee! Fled though, you-yourself with meeting-parting without-way comes. Not fear!
sentences.i: Do not flee. Even if you flee, it will come with you, never parted from you. Do not be afraid.
sentences.n: ma bros cig, 'do not flee' (the other recension has bros shig). 'du 'bral med par, 'without meeting and parting', never apart: the light is not something outside him that he could run from.

sentences.w: ཡི་དྭགས་ ཀྱི་ འོད་ སེར་པོ་ བཀྲག་མེད་ དེ་ ལ་ ཆགས་པར་ མ་ བྱེད་ཅིག༔
sentences.l: Hungry-ghosts' light, yellow, lustreless, that to attachment not do!
sentences.i: Do not be attached to the dull yellow light of the hungry ghosts.
sentences.n: chags par byed, 'to be attached', with ma ... cig, 'do not', like dga' bar byed before.

sentences.w: དེ་ ནི་ འདོད་ཆགས་ དྲག་པོས་ བསགས་པའི་ ཡི་དྭགས་ ཀྱི་ བསུ་བའི་ ལམ་ ཡིན་ནོ༔
sentences.l: That, as-for: desire fierce-by accumulated's hungry-ghosts' welcoming's path it-is.
sentences.i: That is the welcoming path of the hungry ghosts, gathered by fierce desire.
sentences.n: bsags pa'i, 'gathered', stands before yi dwags, where the like sentences of the days before have bag chags, 'habitual tendencies', the thing that is gathered; the other recension has bag chags here too, with de khyod kyi, 'that, your'. The print reads 'the welcoming path of the hungry ghosts gathered by fierce desire', and the translation follows it.

sentences.w: དེ་ ལ་ ཆགས་ ན་ ཁྱོད་ ཡི་དྭགས་ ཀྱིས་ གནས་སུ་ ལྷུང་ ནས་ བཀྲེས་སྐོམ་ གྱི་ སྡུག་བསྔལ་ བཟོད་ གླགས་ མེད་པ་ མྱོང་ སྟེ༔
sentences.l: That to attached if, you, hungry-ghosts'(by?) abode-to fall, then; hunger-thirst's suffering, bearing chance without, experience, and:
sentences.i: If you are attached to it, you will fall into the abode of the hungry ghosts and suffer hunger and thirst past bearing.
sentences.n: yi dwags kyis gnas has kyis, 'by', where kyi, 'of', is meant (the other recension has kyi), as twice above; it is read so. lhung, 'to fall', the print's spelling on the second day. bkres skom, 'hunger and thirst', the torment of the hungry ghosts. bzod glags med pa, 'with no chance to bear it' (bzod, 'to bear'; glags, 'opportunity'), unbearable.

sentences.w: ཐར་ལམ་ བཀག་པའི་ བར་ཆད་ ཡིན་པས༔ དེ་ ལ་ མ་ ཆགས་པར་ ཆགས་སེམས་ སྤོངས་ཤིག༔ མ་ ཞེན་ཅིག༔
sentences.l: Liberation-path blocking's obstacle it-is-because: that to not attached-way, attachment-mind abandon! Not cling!
sentences.i: It is an obstacle that blocks the path to liberation, so do not be attached to it; give up the mind of attachment. Do not cling.
sentences.n: thar lam, 'the path to liberation', thar pa'i lam shortened. For chags sems spongs shig, 'give up the mind of attachment', the other recension has bag chags spongs shig, 'give up the habitual tendencies', as the print had on the third day.

sentences.w: འོད་ དམར་པོ་ གསལ་ ལ་ འཚེར་བ་ དེ་ ལ་ མོས་པ་ གྱིས་ ལ༔ བཅོམ་ལྡན་འདས་ སྣང་བ་མཐའ་ཡས་ ཡབ་ཡུམ་ ལ་ འདུན་པ་ རྩེ་གཅིག་ གཏོད་ ལ༔ སྨོན་ལམ་ འདི་སྐད་དུ་ ཐོབ་ཅིག༔
sentences.l: Light red, bright and shimmering, that to devotion do, and; the Blessed-One Amitābha father-mother to aspiration one-pointed direct, and; prayer these-words-in obtain(?)!
sentences.i: Turn with devotion to the red light, bright and shimmering, direct a single-minded longing to the Blessed One Amitābha and his consort, and make this prayer:
sentences.n: As on the days before. rtse gcig, 'one-pointed', here without the tu of the third day.

sentences.w: ཀྱཻ་མ་ འདོད་ཆགས་ དྲག་པོས་ འཁོར་བར་ འཁྱམས་པའི་ ཚེ༔ / སོར་རྟོགས་ ཡེ་ཤེས་ གསལ་བའི་ འོད་ལམ་ ལ༔ / བཅོམ་ལྡན་ སྣང་བ་མཐའ་ཡས་ ལམ་སྣ་ དྲོངས༔ / ཡུམ་ མཆོག་ གོས་དཀར་མོ་ ཡིས་ རྒྱབ་ ནས་ བསྐྱོར༔ / བར་དོ་ འཇིགས་པའི་ འཕྲང་ ལས་ བསྒྲལ་དུ་ གསོལ༔ / ཡང་དག་ རྫོགས་པའི་ སངས་རྒྱས་ ས་རུ་ བསྐྱོལ༔
sentences.l:
Alas! Desire fierce-by in-saṃsāra wandering's time,
the discerning wisdom bright's light-path on,
the Blessed-One Amitābha the-way lead!
The mother supreme White-Robed-One by from-behind support!
The between fearful's narrow-passage from freeing I-pray;
the genuine perfect buddha's level-to bring!
sentences.i:
Alas! When I wander in saṃsāra through fierce desire,
on the bright light-path of the discriminating wisdom
may the Blessed One Amitābha lead the way,
may the supreme mother, the White-Robed One, support me from behind.
I pray you, free me from the fearful narrow passage of the bardo
and bring me to the level of a true and perfect buddha.
sentences.n: The prayer again, with the fourth day's poison, wisdom, buddha and consort. sor rtogs ye shes is so sor rtogs pa'i ye shes, shortened for the metre. The consort has yis, 'by', as on the first day. bskyol is the print's spelling here of skyol, 'bring!', with a prefixed b- (the other recension has skyol).

sentences.w: དེ་སྐད་ མོས་གུས་ དྲག་པོས་ སྨོན་ལམ་ བཏབ་པས༔ བཅོམ་ལྡན་འདས་ སྣང་བ་མཐའ་ཡས་ འོད་དཔག་མེད་ ཀྱི་ ཐུགས་ཀར་ འཇའ་འོད་དུ་ ཐིམ་ ནས༔ ནུབ་ཕྱོགས་ བདེ་བ་ཅན་ གྱི་ ཞིང་ཁམས་སུ་ ལོངས་སྤྱོད་རྫོགས་པའི་སྐུ་རུ་ སངས་རྒྱས་པར་ འགྱུར་རོ༔
sentences.l: Those-words, devotion-respect fierce-by, prayer made-because: the Blessed-One Amitābha Measureless-Light's heart-in as-rainbow-light dissolving, then, the west-direction, the-Blissful's realm-in, as-the-body-of-perfect-enjoyment buddha becomes.
sentences.i: When he makes the prayer in these words with fierce devotion, he dissolves as rainbow light into the heart of the Blessed One Amitābha, Measureless Light, and becomes a buddha in the body of perfect enjoyment in the western realm of Bliss.
sentences.n: As on the third day. 'Od dpag med, 'Measureless Light', is the usual Tibetan name of Amitābha; here the print gives both names. The other recension adds yab yum, 'and his consort'.

sentences.l: By-that, as-for: not freed not possible.
sentences.i: It is impossible that he will not be freed by this.
sentences.n: mi srid, 'it cannot be, it is impossible': mi grol mi srid, 'not to be freed is impossible', a double negative that makes a firm assurance.

sentences.w: ཡང་ དེ་ལྟར་དུ་ ངོ་སྤྲད་ ཀྱང་ སེམས་ཅན་ བག་ཆགས་ དང་ འགྲོགས་ ཡུན་རིང་པའི་ སྟབས་ ཀྱིས་ བག་ཆགས་ མི་ སྤོང་བར་ ཕྲག་དོག་ དང་ ལས་ངན་ གྱི་ དབང་ གིས་ སྒྲ་ འོད་ ལ་ དངངས་སྐྲག་ སྐྱེས་ ཏེ༔
sentences.l: Again, thus face-introduced though: beings, habitual-tendencies with associating long's because-of, habitual-tendencies not abandoning-way, jealousy and bad-karma's power by, sound, light at dread-terror arisen, and:
sentences.i: But though they are pointed out in this way, beings who have long kept company with their habitual tendencies do not give them up, and through the force of jealousy and bad karma dread and terror arise in them at the sounds and lights.
sentences.n: sems can, 'sentient being', any being with a mind. 'grogs, 'to keep company with'; yun ring pa, 'long-lasting'; stabs kyis, 'because of, by reason of'. phrag dog, 'jealousy, envy', is the poison of the fifth day. dngangs skrag, 'dread and terror', one word like 'jigs skrag; dngangs is the print's spelling of sngangs, as in 003.

sentences.w: ཐུགས་རྗེའི་ འོད་ཟེར་ གྱི་ ལྕགས་ཀྱུས་ མི་ ཟིན་པར༔ ཞག་ ལྔ་པའི་ བར་དུ་ མར་ ལ་ འཁྱམས་ ཏེ༔
sentences.l: Compassion's light-ray's iron-hook-by not seized-way, day fifth's until, downward wander, and:
sentences.i: They are not caught by the hook of the light of compassion, and wander on down to the fifth day.
sentences.n: lcags kyus, 'by the hook', kyu with -s. mi zin par, 'without being caught'. zhag lnga pa'i bar du, 'until the fifth day'. mar la, 'downward', the opposite of yar la, 'upward': the dead go on down through the days.

sentences.w: ཡང་ དེའི་ ཚེ་ བཅོམ་ལྡན་འདས་ དོན་ཡོད་གྲུབ་པའི་ ལྷ་ཚོགས་ ཐུགས་རྗེའི་ འོད་ཟེར་ དང་ བཅས་ཏེ་ བསུ་བ་ ལ་ བྱོན་ནོ༔
sentences.l: Again, that's time: the Blessed-One Amoghasiddhi's deity-host, compassion's light-rays with together, meeting for came.
sentences.i: Then the host of deities of the Blessed One Amoghasiddhi comes to meet them, with the rays of compassion.
sentences.n: Don yod grub pa, 'He Whose Aim Is Accomplished' (Sanskrit Amoghasiddhi; don yod, 'not in vain'; grub pa, 'accomplished'), is the buddha of the north and of the fifth day. dang bcas te, 'together with'. byon, 'came', the respectful word for the coming of a buddha; byon no closes the sentence, where the other recension runs on with te.

sentences.w: ཉོན་མོངས་པ་ ཕྲག་དོག་ ལས་ གྲུབ་པའི་ ལྷ་མ་ཡིན་ གྱི་ འོད་ལམ་ གྱིས་ ཀྱང་ བསུ་བ་ ལ་ འོང་ངོ༔
sentences.l: Affliction jealousy from formed's demigods' light-path by also, meeting for comes.
sentences.i: The light-path of the demigods, formed from the affliction of jealousy, also comes to meet them.
sentences.n: nyon mongs pa, 'affliction, disturbing emotion' (Sanskrit kleśa), the name for the poisons of the mind. lha ma yin, 'not-gods', the demigods (Sanskrit asura), who war with the gods out of envy; theirs is the realm this day's dull light leads to.

sentences.w: དེའི་ ཚེ་ ཡང་ ངོ་སྤྲད་པ་ ནི༔ ཚེ་འདས་ ཀྱི་ མིང་ ནས་ འབོད་ ལ་ འདི་སྐད་དོ༔ ཀྱཻ་ རིགས་ཀྱི་བུ༔ མ་ ཡེངས་པར་ ཉོན་ཅིག༔
sentences.l: That's time also, the face-introduction, as-for: the dead-one's by-name calling, and, these-words: O child-of-noble-family! Not distracted-way listen!
sentences.i: At that time point him out again. Call the dead person by name and say this: O child of noble family, listen without distraction.
sentences.n: As on the days before; here the print writes 'bod with its first letter.

sentences.w: ཞག་ ལྔ་པ་ ལ་ འབྱུང་བ་ རླུང་ ཐམས་ཅད་ རྣམ་པར་ དག་པའི་ འོད་ ལྗང་ཁུ་ འཆར་རོ༔
sentences.l: Day fifth on, element wind all completely pure's light, green, dawns.
sentences.i: On the fifth day the green light dawns, the light of the element wind, all of it wholly purified.
sentences.n: rlung, 'wind', the element of movement. ljang khu, 'green'. The other recension again has no thams cad, 'all'.

sentences.w: དེའི་ དུས་སུ་ བྱང་ཕྱོགས་ ལས་ རབ་བརྩེགས་པའི་ ཞིང་ཁམས་ ལྗང་ཁུ་ ནས༔ བཅོམ་ལྡན་འདས་ སངས་རྒྱས་ དོན་ཡོད་གྲུབ་པ་ གཙོ་འཁོར་ སྐུ་མདོག་ ལྗང་ཁུ་ ཕྱག་ ན་ རྡོ་རྗེ་རྒྱ་གྲམ་ བསྣམས་པ༔
sentences.l: That's time-at, the north-direction from, Heaped-Up's realm, green, from: the Blessed-One Buddha Amoghasiddhi, chief-retinue, body-colour green, hand in crossed-vajra holding,
sentences.i: At that time, from the north, from the green realm called Heaped Up, the Blessed One, the Buddha Amoghasiddhi, chief and retinue, green in colour, holding a crossed vajra in his hand,
sentences.n: byang phyogs, 'the north', here with las, 'from', as well as the nas after the realm. Rab brtsegs pa, 'Heaped Up, Piled High' (rab, 'very'; brtsegs, 'stacked'), is the print's name for the northern buddha-field; the other recension has Rab rdzogs pa, 'Fully Accomplished'. The letters of the print are clear. gtso 'khor, 'chief and retinue', the buddha with those around him; only the print has it here. rdo rje rgya gram, 'crossed vajra' (rgya gram, 'cross'), two vajras laid across each other, the emblem of the north.

sentences.w: ནམ་མཁའ་ལྡིང་ ཤང་ཤང་ གི་ ཁྲི་ ལ་ བཞུགས་པ༔ ཡུམ་ དམ་ཚིག་སྒྲོལ་མ་ དང་ ཞལ་སྦྱར་ ནས་ ཁྱོད་རང་ ལ་ འཆར་དུ་ འོང་ངོ༔
sentences.l: Sky-soaring shang-shang's throne on seated, the mother Commitment-Tārā with face-joined, then, you-yourself to dawning comes.
sentences.i: seated on a throne of shang-shang birds that soar in the sky, in union with his consort Samayatārā, dawns before you.
sentences.n: nam mkha' lding, 'soaring in the sky', is the name of the garuḍa, the great bird; shang shang is a winged creature of the same kind, in pictures part bird and part human; the throne of the north is borne by them (the other recension has mkha' lding). The print has ཁྲིལ, with no tsheg to be seen between khri, 'throne', and la, 'on': a worn tsheg cannot be ruled out, and khri la, which the sense needs and the other recension has, is read, but it is uncertain. Dam tshig sgrol ma, 'Tārā of the Commitment' (Sanskrit Samayatārā; sgrol ma, 'she who frees'), is the consort of the north. The part ends here; the fifth day's bodhisattvas begin the next.
